terms.gloss: drive out or away; rout (an enemy)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; the place with the ablative alone or with ex, dē, or ab
evidence: Cic. Pis. 23: cum virī bonī lapidibus ē forō pellerentur (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 1.40: sē patriō rēgnō pulsōs esse (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its first sense is to strike or beat: terram pede pellere, to stamp the ground (Lucr. 5.1402, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Pis. 16: mē domō meā expulistis (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fin. 1.37: cum cibō et pōtiōne famēs sitisque dēpulsa est (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Caecin. 49: dēmovērī et dēpellī dē locō (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: put to flight, drive away, rout
evidence: Caes. BG 7.68.1: fugātō omnī equitātū (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: send or drive off, remove; clear (a crowd) out of the way
evidence: Tac. Agr. 23: submōtīs velut in aliam īnsulam hostibus (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: cum virī bonī lapidibus ē forō pellerentur
phrases.english: when good men were being driven from the forum with stones
you drove me out of my own house

phrases.latin: cum cibō et pōtiōne famēs sitisque dēpulsa est
phrases.english: when hunger and thirst have been driven off by food and drink
when all the cavalry had been put to flight

phrases.latin: submōtīs velut in aliam īnsulam hostibus
phrases.english: the enemy having been pushed back, as it were, into another island

sources: Lewis & Short: pello · Lewis & Short: expello
Lewis & Short: fugo
